Petition under Section 166 and 140 of M.V. Act, 1988  for grant of compensation AWARD 1.

The petitioners have sought compensation to the tune of Rs. 3,00,00,000/- with interest from the date of filing of petition till the date of realization, for the fatal injury sustained by Smt. Deepti Pandey in Motor Vehicular Accident which occurred on 01.02.2014 at about 9:15 AM, near Katra,
Jalalabad Road, in front of Bharat Petrol Pump, involving Car bearing temporary registration no.
DL13C-7132 being driven by respondent no. 1 in a rash and negligent manner.

2. It is averred in the claim petition that on 01.02.2014 at about 9:15 am, Smt. Deepti Pandey (deceased herein) alongwith her relative and friend were travelling/proceeding towards Delhi Road at her native place at MACP No. 6606/16; FIR No. 69/14 DOD: 07.03.2026 Vasundara by car bearing temporary registration no. DL13C-7132.

When they reached near Katra, Jalalabad Road, in front of Bharat Petrol Pump, one unknown vehicle which was being driven by its driver at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, came from Katra Side and hit against the aforesaid car,
as a result of which, driver of said Honda Car lost its control and collided with the tree and fell down in deep valley, due to which occupants of the car sustained serious/grievous injuries.
They were immediately taken to Siddhi Vinayak Hospital, Civil Lines, Bareilly, UP.

FIR No. 69/14, u/s.
279/337/338/304A/427 IPC was registered at PS. Katra with regard to the said accident.

The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no.
3/Universal Sompo General Insurance Company Limited during the period in question.

sentences.text: 3. In his written statement, the respondent no. 1 i.e., driver raised preliminary objection by claiming that he has been falsely implicated in the alleged accident as he has nothing to do with the accident.

He further claimed that the accident, if any took place only due to the negligence of Sh. Saurabh Pandey who was the husband of respondent no. 2.

He also claimed that alleged offending vehicle was insured with respondent no. 3 at the time of accident and thus, insurance company is liable to pay compensation,
if any to the petitioner.
He denied the averments made in the claim petition and prayed for its dismissal.

2 4. In her written statement, the respondent no. 2 i.e., registered owner claimed that present claim petition is not maintainable being filed in collusion between the claimant and driver (respondent no.
1) because respondent no. 1 was not driving the offending vehicle and he was also travelling in the alleged offending vehicle which was damaged by some other truck that fled away from the spot of accident.
She further claimed that present case was a hit and run case and offending vehicle could not be identified and was not traceable as per final report file by IO.
She further claimed that alleged offending vehicle was being driven by deceased Saurabh Pandey at the time of accident.
On the basis of these averments, she prayed for dismissal of present claim petition.
5. Respondent no. 3/insurance company has raised preliminary objections that present claim petition is not maintainable.

It has claimed that as per the police report, present case was hit and run case as unknown vehicle had hit the alleged offending vehicle, due to which occupants of the alleged offending vehicle sustained injuries.

It is further claimed that present claim is liable to be dismissed as the alleged offending vehicle was having only temporary registration number and was not having permanent registration number which was in violation of M.V. Act.

It is further claimed that driver of the alleged offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and thus, insurance company is not liable to pay compensation, if any to the petitioner.
However, it has admitted that the offending vehicle was insured with it at the time of accident.
On merits, it has denied the averments made in the claim petition and prayed for its dismissal.

From pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed vide order dated 04.05.2017 passed by Ld. Predecessor:-
1.

Whether the injured Deepti Pandey suffered injuries in road traffic accident on 01.02.2014 at about 9:15 am, in front of Bharat Petrol Pump, Jalalabad Road, District Shahjahan Pur, UP, within the jurisdiction of PS. Katra, District Shahjahanpur, UP,
due to rashness and negligence on the part of the driver Arun who was driving vehicle bearing registration no. DL13C-7132, owned by Swati Pandey and insured with Universal Sompo General Insurance Co. Ltd?OPP.
2.

7. To substantiate their claim, petitioners have examined eight witnesses i.e. Sh. Sandip Kumar Trivedi (husband of deceased injured) as PW1, Dr. M.Q. Ansari, CMO, Siddhi Vinayak Hospital, UP as PW2, Sh. R.P. Pandey (father of deceased injured) as PW3, Dr. Sapna Ramani Sardana as PW4,
Dr. Samir Kumar Kalra as PW5, Sh. Vikas Kumar(from the office of college of deceased injured) as Sandeep Kumar vs Arun And Ors

3 PW6, Sh. Gaurav Malhotra, Record Officer, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital as PW7 and SI Mahendra Singh (IO of the case) as PW8 and closed their evidence on 05.10.2023.
The respondent no. 1 i.e., driver has examined himself as R1W1.
On the other hand, no evidence was adduced by remaining respondents and RE in the matter was closed vide order dated 28.11.2025.

I have heard arguments advanced by learned counsel for the LR of injured(now deceased) and learned counsel for insurance company and have gone through the documents filed alongwith the present claim petition.
9. It is pertinent to mention that none of the witness examined by the petitioner is an eyewitness.
However, the testimony of PW8 IO SI Mahendra Singh is relevant as he conducted the investigation in the present case.
He has deposed that he was the IO of the case FIR No. 69/14, PS. Katra, District Shahjahanpur, UP, U/s. 279/338/427/304A IPC.
He further deposed that he had filed the final report before the concerned court.
He further deposed that the FIR was registered on the written complaint of Sh. Anurag Pandey(brother of deceased Deepti Pandey).
He collectively marked the copies of complaint, Rojnamcha, site plan and final report as Mark A(Colly).
He further deposed that no eyewitness was available at the spot of accident, therefore, he had not recorded the statement of any eyewitness.

He volunteered that information of accident was received from PS,
after occurrence of the accident.
He deposed that he investigated the matter after the same was handed over to him on registration of FIR and was not able to find any eyewitness despite efforts.
During his cross-examination on behalf of driver, he denied the suggestion that he extricated the body of deceased who was in the victim vehicle i.e., Honda Amaze at the seat behind the driver.
He deposed that the collision of the victim vehicle was head on.
He further deposed that despite investigation, it could not be established whether the victim vehicle was hit by any other vehicle or not.
He volunteered that the MACP No. 6606/16; FIR No. 69/14 DOD: 07.03.2026 vehicle was found having climbed over a tree by the roadside on the side on which victim was travelling.
He denied the suggestion that Arun Singh was not the driver of the Honda Amaze which met with an accident.
He volunteered that as per complaint lodged by Anurag Pandey, brother of deceased, Arun Singh was the driver of the vehicle.
He volunteered that at the time of final report as hit and run case, the deceased Deepti Trivedi for whom the present claim was pending was shown as injured in the road accident in question.
10. Therefore, the testimony of PW8 shows that the final report was untrace as some other vehicle had hit the car due to which the accident took place.

Even otherwise, a bare perusal of copy of FIR (which is part of criminal case record Ex. PW1/3 colly) reveals that the same was recorded on the statement of Sh. Anurag Pandey (brother of deceased), wherein he categorically stated that an unknown vehicle had hit the aforesaid Honda Amaze Car and ran away from the spot after causing the accident.

11. Bare perusal of para no. 2 of affidavit in evidence of PW1 (husband of deceased) shows that he has stated that some unknown vehicle suddenly hit the vehicle in which deceased persons were travelling which was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, at a very high speed, due to Sandeep Kumar vs Arun And Ors on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118264745/
4 which the vehicle in which deceased persons were travelling, lost its control and struck down against the tree and dumped in deep yards.

sentences.text: Further, affidavit in evidence of PW3 who is father of deceased also reveals the same fact in para no. 2 of his affidavit.

Therefore, it is the case of petitioner himself MACP No. 6606/16; FIR No. 69/14 DOD: 07.03.2026 that as some unknown vehicle was rash and negligent, it hit the car (in which the victim was travelling and due to which, it lost control).

In such a scenario, where negligence, rash driving of unknown vehicle is claimed by the petitioners then it does not show or prove any negligence on the part of driver of car, as according to the petitioner,
this car lost control only when hit by unknown vehicle.
In order to prove the negligence of driver of car, i.e., respondent no. 1, nothing has been brought on record by the petitioners to prove the same.
12. On the other hand, the respondent no. 1/driver of alleged offending vehicle has examined himself as R1W1.
As already mentioned above, Sh. Arun was one of the occupants of the offending vehicle which fact has not been disputed by the respondents also.
Thus, he is one of the material witnesses being the only eyewitness alive after the accident.
13. R1W1 Sh. Arun has deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. R1W1/A) that accident did not take place due to his negligent driving of alleged offending vehicle.

He further deposed that he was not the driver of alleged offending vehicle and husband of respondent no. 2 namely Sh. Saurabh Pandey was driving the same at the time of accident and he was sitting on front seat of the alleged offending vehicle besides the seat of driver.

He further deposed that Sh. Saurabh Pandey who was driving the vehicle in question in a rash and negligent manner, suddenly crossed a truck and lost control over his vehicle and hit the same against a tree.
He further deposed that the entire details of the accident had been published in the newspaper.

He MACP No. 6606/16; FIR No. 69/14 DOD:
07.03.2026 has relied upon copy of his Aadhaar Card as Ex. R1W1/1 and copy of newspaper cutting dated 02.02.2014 marked as Mark A. During his cross- examination on behalf of petitioner, he deposed that the accident had occurred on 01.02.2014.
He further deposed that the car bearing registration no. DL13C-7132 was being driven by Mr. Saurabh.
He further deposed that he used to drive four wheeler occasionally.
He further deposed that he did not know as to who was taking back the aforesaid car from the home of Swati Pandey to Shahjahanpur, UP, where Mr. Saurabh was residing.

He further deposed that on the date and time of accident, Mr. Saurabh asked him to come with him to Delhi for touring purpose and also stated that since he knew the driving, Saurabh would get rest when he would drive the aforesaid car.

He deposed that he did not know whether Mr.
Saurabh was having driving licence at the time of accident or not.
He further deposed that he knew Mr. Saurabh from last 20-22 years as he was residing in their neighbourhood.
He further deposed that there were total four occupants in the aforesaid car at the time of accident.
He further deposed that he was sitting just besides the driver's seat, Mrs. Bisariya was sitting just behind the driver's seat and Mrs. Deepti Pandey was sitting behind his seat.
14. During his cross-examination on behalf of insurance company, he admitted that entire incident of accident was published in the newspaper which was exhibited as Ex. R1W1/R3X.
He further deposed that he had not handed over the copy of aforesaid newspaper to the police as the police was already aware of the entire incident and was having the copy of aforesaid newspaper.

He further deposed that he was sitting in the front adjacent seat of MACP No. 6606/16; FIR No. 69/14 DOD:
07.03.2026 the driver.

He further deposed that he had suffered injuries in the said accident and he Sandeep Kumar vs Arun And Ors on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118264745/
5 was got treated for the said injuries.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He deposed that the vehicle in question was being driven by late Sh. Saurabh Pandey on the day of incident and he died because of the injuries suffered by him in the said accident.
He further deposed that he was not possessing any driving licence at the time of incident as he never applied for the same.
He further deposed that the vehicle in question was private vehicle.

15. Hence, the respondent no. 1 denied being the driver of car and rather stated that Saurabh Pandey, brother of deceased was driving the car and as he crossed a truck, he lost control and hit against a tree.

16. From the aforesaid testimonies of PWs and RWs, it is clear that petitioners have not been able to prove any negligence of driver of car, once admittedly, it was hit by some unknown vehicle, which was rash and negligent.
The petitioner has not adduced any evidence in rebuttal of final report filed by the investigating officer to the effect that the aforesaid Honda Amaze Car was hit by some unknown vehicle.

The petitioner has also failed to file any protest petition before the concerned court to the effect that he is not satisfied with the untrace report or that driver of the victim's car was negligent in driving.

17. Hence, in view of above discussion it is held that the petitioners have failed to prove even on the principles of preponderance of probabilities that the deceased Smt. Deepti Pandey, suffered fatal injuries in the accident MACP No. 6606/16; FIR No. 69/14 DOD: 07.03.2026 which occurred on 01.02.2014 at about 9:15 AM, near Katra, Jalalabad Road, in front of Bharat Petrol Pump, due to rash and negligent driving of Honda Amaze Car bearing temporary registration no. DL13C-7132 by respondent no. 1 Sh. Arun.
Issue no.1 is accordingly decided in favour of respondents and against the petitioners.
ISSUE NO.2 18.

In view of findings on issue no.1(supra), it is clear that the petitioners have failed to prove the negligence on the part of driver of Honda Amaze Car bearing temporary registration no.
DL13C-7132.

Since, this is a claim petition under Section 166 and 140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and the petitioner has failed to prove the negligence on the part of driver of offending Car, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities, hence he is not entitled to any compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act.
19. In view of findings on issues no.1 and 2 (supra), present claim petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is dismissed.
Copy be given dasti.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
